To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the thalamic response to a single electrical pulse consists in an immediate firing of a few cells, followed by a progressive activation of the remaining cells.
the response of a thalamic neuronal population electrically stimulated is characterized by a high degree of heterogeneity, and is modified in a complex way upon repetition of the stimuli.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following problems: (1) the spatial distribution of the different types of responses to a local stimulation; (2) the changes in the responses to a repeated stimulation at 100 msec interval, and (3) the changes in responses to a repeated local stimulation of VL in the decorticate preparation and of the GM in intact cats.
the study of the response of thalamic cell populations to electrical stimulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in thalamic cells, the response pattern is not a function of the stimulus parameters, but of the anatomical location of the stimulated site and of the cell under study.

the thalamic cell response to electrical stimulation is a function of the stimulus parameters (intensity and duration), of the anatomical location of the stimulated site, and of the distance of the cells of the recording site.
the thalamic cells are not immediately silenced by the electrical stimulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thalamus is a highly organized and differentiated structure.

, in the thalamus, the immediate effect of an electric shock applied to a given cell is to silence a large proportion of the cells in its vicinity, and that this effect is not confined to the immediate vicinity, but is propagated to more distant cells.

the response of the thalamic population to local stimulation is characterized by a high proportion of non-responsive cells, and that this response is not uniform, but rather varies with the cell location.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immediate silencing of cells in the vicinity of a thalamic stimulation is a general feature of the thalamic cell populations.
the response of thalamic neurons to electrical stimulation depends on a number of parameters, including the location of the cell with respect to the stimulating electrode.
the immediate silence of thalamic cells is not a specific property of the VL.
